html:
Afonso Henriques was the first king of Portugal. He turned the County of Portugal, a fief of the kingdom of León, into an independent kingdom.

He took power in 1128 after defeating his mother's forces at São Mamede, near Guimarães, now called the cradle of the nation. After a victory over the Moors at Ourique in 1139 he called himself king. León recognised him in 1143, and the pope in 1179.

He pushed the border south against al-Andalus, taking Santarém and, with the help of crusaders, Lisbon in the siege of 1147. By his death in 1185 Portugal reached south of the Tagus. Its borders were complete by 1249, earlier than almost any other European state, part of the wider Reconquista.
